question: For Toyota Motor Corporation's FY2027 first quarter (April 1 - June 30, 2026; Toyota's fiscal year ends March 31), what were consolidated operating income and net income attributable to Toyota shareholders in yen, what is the company's revised FY2027 operating income forecast versus its previous (May 2026) forecast, and which line items explain why net income rose strongly while operating income fell?
grading: Key points (all required): (1) Q1 FY2027 operating income about JPY 1,063.5 billion (JPY 1,063,473 million; accept 1,063.4-1,063.5), down 8.8% y/y; (2) net income attributable to Toyota JPY 1,477.0 billion (+75.6%); (3) revised FY2027 operating income forecast JPY 3.4 trillion versus JPY 3.0 trillion previously; (4) explanation: income before income taxes was JPY 1,963.9 billion (+56.8%), about JPY 900 billion above operating income, helped by other finance income (JPY 850.6 billion vs 153.7 billion a year earlier), equity-method profit (JPY 210.7 billion) and a foreign-exchange gain (JPY 112.4 billion vs a JPY 212.4 billion loss), partly offset by other finance costs (JPY 285.6 billion). Fail if the answer states the quarter as calendar 2027 or Jan-Mar, uses the May forecast (JPY 3.0 trillion) as current, or says net income fell.
answer: Q1 FY2027 (April 1-June 30, 2026): sales revenues JPY 13,525.4 billion (+10.4%); operating income JPY 1,063.5 billion (-8.8% from JPY 1,166.1 billion); income before income taxes JPY 1,963.9 billion (+56.8%); net income attributable to Toyota JPY 1,477.0 billion (+75.6%) [W10-E1]. The gap is non-operating: other finance income of JPY 850.6 billion (JPY 153.7 billion a year earlier), equity-method profit JPY 210.7 billion and a JPY 112.4 billion FX gain (vs a JPY 212.4 billion loss), less JPY 285.6 billion of other finance costs [W10-E1]. The FY2027 forecast was raised on 4 August to operating income JPY 3.4 trillion (from JPY 3.0 trillion), net income JPY 3.25 trillion (from 3.0 trillion) and sales JPY 54.0 trillion (from 51.0 trillion), with USD/JPY assumed at 160 (from 150) [W10-E2].

**Question:** For Toyota Motor Corporation's FY2027 first quarter (April 1 - June 30, 2026; Toyota's fiscal year ends March 31), what were consolidated operating income and net income attributable to Toyota shareholders in yen, what is the company's revised FY2027 operating income forecast versus its previous (May 2026) forecast, and which line items explain why net income rose strongly while operating income fell?
*As of 2026-10-03*

**Interpreted as:** Question's 'FY2027' = Toyota's fiscal year ending March 31, 2027; the calendar labels this same year 'FY2026' (2026-04-01 to 2027-03-31). Q1 = the quarter April 1 - June 30, 2026, reported ~early August 2026 (already reported as of today, 2026-10-03). 'Net income attributable to Toyota shareholders' = net income attributable to Toyota Motor Corporation. 'Previous (May 2026) forecast' = the full-year FY2027 operating income guidance issued with the FY2026 full-year results in May 2026. Toyota does not file quarterly results with the SEC, so Q1 figures and the revised outlook are read from the earnings release and web coverage.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) | 1,063,473 [1] | 1,477,044 [1] | 13,525,400 [1] | 1,963,862 [1] | 1,551,725 [1] | — | — | — | — | — |
| Q1 FY2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2025) | 1,166,141 [1] | 841,345 [1] | — | 1,252,152 [1] | 872,193 [1] | — | — | — | — | — |
| FY2027 forecast — previous (May 2026) | — | — | — | — | — | 3,000.0 [2] | — | 51,000.0 [2] | — | 5.9 [2] |
| FY2027 forecast — revised (August 4, 2026) | — | — | — | — | — | 3,400.0 [2] | — | 54,000.0 [2] | — | 6.3 [2] |
| FY2027 forecast — change | — | — | — | — | — | — | +400.0 [2] | — | +3,000.0 [2] | — |

- Toyota's Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) consolidated operating income was ¥1,063,473 million (1,063.4 billion yen), a decrease of 102.6 billion yen, or 8.8%, from ¥1,166,141 million in Q1 FY2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2025); the calculated year-over-year change is -8.8%. [1]
- Toyota's Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) net income attributable to Toyota Motor Corporation was ¥1,477,044 million (1,477.0 billion yen), an increase of 635.6 billion yen, or 75.6%, from ¥841,345 million in Q1 FY2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2025); the calculated year-over-year change is 75.6%. [1]
- Toyota's revised FY2027 (year ending March 31, 2027) full-year operating income forecast, issued with the Q1 results on August 4, 2026, is ¥3,400.0 billion, raised by ¥400.0 billion from the previous forecast of ¥3,000.0 billion given with the May 2026 FY2026 full-year results. [2][3][4]
- Alongside the operating income upgrade, Toyota's FY2027 forecast lifts sales revenues to ¥54,000.0 billion from ¥51,000.0 billion (a ¥3,000.0 billion increase) and the forecast operating margin to 6.3% from 5.9%. [2]
- Toyota attributed the Q1 FY2027 operating income decline to these changes: marketing efforts +¥70.0 billion, effects of changes in exchange rates +¥345.0 billion, cost reduction efforts -¥85.0 billion, increase or decrease in expenses and expense reduction efforts -¥190.0 billion, and other -¥242.6 billion, which sum to -102.6 billion yen, matching the reported 102.6 billion yen decline. [1]
- The line items that explain why Q1 FY2027 net income rose while operating income fell are below-the-line items: other finance income rose to ¥850,594 million from ¥153,721 million, foreign exchange gain (loss), net swung to a gain of ¥112,378 million from a loss of ¥212,375 million, and share of profit of investments accounted for using the equity method rose to ¥210,685 million from ¥141,044 million, while income tax expense rose only to ¥412,136 million from ¥379,959 million. [1]
- Secondary coverage of the August 4, 2026 release said the net profit jump was driven largely by currency gains and non-operating income rather than core automotive performance, with other financial income surging from 153.7 billion yen to 850.5 billion yen partly on a one-time gain tied to the privatization of Toyota Industries, and noted the operating margin narrowed to 7.9% from 9.5% a year earlier. [5]
